title: Large Language Model-Aided Partial Program Dependence Analysis
summary: ΛMDA is a two-phase framework for analysing partial Java programs that cannot be compiled. Phase 1 (Context Augmentation): an LLM receives a partial Java snippet together with compiler error messages iteratively, producing an approximately-complete program P_AC that compiles. Two prompts are used — an initial approximation prompt and a self-correction prompt that feeds back the compiler error. Phase 2 (Analysis): Joern runs on P_AC to produce a Program Dependence Graph (PDG). Edges are then pruned to retain only those whose both endpoints are statements present in the original partial snippet P, giving a PDG over the original code.

This reproduction replaces Phase 1 with a single Claude Sonnet 4.6 call per snippet using two prompt strategies: a black-box prompt (Prompt A) that asks the model to produce an approximately-complete Java class, and an informed prompt (Prompt B) that describes the 6-step methodology (import resolution, type inference, stub generation, compilation fix, wrapping, output format). Phase 2 (Joern analysis and edge pruning) is kept identical to the paper.

dataset.name: StatType-SO
dataset.description: 172 partial Java code snippets collected from StackOverflow, annotated with manually-completed ground-truth programs and their PDGs.
dataset.reason_for_choice: StatType-SO is the smaller of the two paper datasets (172 vs 274 for COSTER-SO), chosen for cost efficiency. It is also the primary dataset in the paper's main evaluation (Table 1).

metric.note: Evaluated on DDG (data dependence) edges only. This corresponds to the 'Data' column in the paper's Table 1, NOT the headline 'Data+Control' column. The paper's calculate_fp_tp_fn function (from RQ3_eval.py) is reproduced verbatim.

original_result.note: Computed by our evaluator on pre-stored PrePA_code_res PDGs from Stattype_res.json, using the same calculate_fp_tp_fn function as the paper. Covers n=109 entries that have valid DDG edges in partial_code (not the paper's own n=164 count). These numbers correspond to the 'Data' column of Table 1, not the Data+Control headline.

our_result.structural_gap: Single LLM call only — no iterative compiler feedback loop. The paper's self-correction phase (feeding compiler errors back to the LLM across multiple iterations) is absent.
